justification: One data file is added and no code changes. plan_brief_checks.brief_recall reads data/plan_brief_gold_holdout.json, and without it the check reports unknown on main. A wrong file could make the recall number wrong, which is why the check also reads the proven rules from the database and the file only adds the held-out councils.

pre_impl.existing_data: plan_brief_checks.brief_recall joins this file's ids to regulatory_provisions and compares them with project_brief_rows.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If an id in the file is no longer a current clause it does not match any brief row, and the recall number goes down, not up, so a stale file cannot inflate the result.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to the next run of the check only. No table or row is written.

residual_risk: The file was produced by the applies-when session from the councils' own plans and was not independently read. The check reports hold-out recall separately from the tuning councils, 94 percent on 50 cases, with a 95 percent lower bound of 84 percent against a bar of 90 percent, so the hold-out figure alone does not prove the bar.

break_it.scenario: The file holds an id for a clause that has since been withdrawn or re-extracted under a new id.
break_it.what_happens: That rule no longer matches any brief row, so the hold-out recall goes down and the check can fail. It cannot report a higher number than the truth.
break_it.how: scripts/plan_brief_checks.py:98 reads this file and joins its ids to current, actionable clauses, so a stale id counts as a miss.
break_it.repro: python scripts/plan_brief_checks.py via brief_recall(), after withdrawing one clause id listed in the file
